description: NixOS Package PRs for ksshaskpass, udisks-2.9.4, accountsservice, e2fsprogs-1.46.6, linux-pam-1.5.2, cups-2.4.2 packages on GitHub

items.content_html:
Issue

I found a crash in accounts-daemon that only affects NixOS systems with users.mutableUsers = false. It is caused by a nixpkgs patch.

Who is impacted?

NixOS systems with users.mutableUsers = false and services.accounts-daemon.enable = true. GNOME, COSMIC, Cinnamon, Pantheon and LightDM enable the daemon.

Reproudction

{
  nixpkgs ? ./.,
}:
let
  pkgs = import nixpkgs { };
in
pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest {
  name = "as-crash";
  nodes.immutable = {
    services.accounts-daemon.enable = true;
    security.polkit.enable = true;
    users.mutableUsers = false;
    users.allowNoPasswordLogin = true;
    users.users.alice = {
      isNormalUser = true;
    };
  };
  testScript = ''
    immutable.start_job("accounts-daemon.service")
    immutable.wait_for_unit("accounts-daemon.service")
    pid = immutable.succeed("systemctl show -p MainPID --value accounts-daemon").strip()
    for method in ["SetRealName s Eve", "SetShell s /bin/sh", "SetPassword ss x y"]:
        print("### alice " + method + ": " + immutable.execute(f"su - alice -c 'busctl call -- org.freedesktop.Accounts /org/freedesktop/Accounts/User1000 org.freedesktop.Accounts.User {method}' 2>&1")[1])
        immutable.sleep(2)
        print("### MainPID " + immutable.execute("systemctl show -p MainPID -p NRestarts -p ActiveState accounts-daemon | tr '\\n' ' '")[1])
    print("### coredumps: " + immutable.execute("coredumpctl list --no-pager 2>&1 | tail -n +2 | wc -l")[1])
    print("### start pid " + pid)
  '';
}
$ nix-build accountsservice-crash.nix --arg nixpkgs 'fetchTarball "https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/archive/9861f4a9fe3d.tar.gz"' --no-out-link

### alice SetPassword ss x y: Call failed: Modifying users not supported without users.mutableUsers
### MainPID ActiveState=failed MainPID=0 NRestarts=0 
### coredumps: 3
### start pid 548

Commits

  • accountsservice: return TRUE from methods disabled for immutable users

The D-Bus method handlers return gboolean, but the guards in Disable-methods-that-change-files-in-etc.patch end with a bare return. GDBus then gets an undefined value after the error reply is sent.

With users.mutableUsers = false, a call such as SetRealName on one's own account crashes accounts-daemon in g_object_unref. GCC 14 reports this as an error, and -Wno-error=return-mismatch hid it.

The package now builds without that flag and without the other two GCC 14 workarounds.

  • accountsservice: reject account type, expiration and auto-login changes when users are immutable

SetAccountType runs usermod, SetPasswordExpirationPolicy and SetUserExpirationPolicy run chage, and SetAutomaticLogin writes the display manager config. With users.mutableUsers = false, activation overwrites these changes. SetPasswordExpirationPolicy also lets users change the password aging of their own account without admin rights (accountsservice!190).

Return the same NotSupported error as the other disabled methods.

  • nixos/accountsservice: sandbox accounts-daemon when users are immutable (ref #377827)

The upstream unit gives the daemon write access to /etc and the home folders, and every capability, for the shadow tools it runs. With users.mutableUsers = false, every method is disabled.

Now we remove write access to /etc and the home folders, keep only CAP_SETUID and CAP_SETGID for reading icons as the caller, and add NoNewPrivileges, a system call filter and protection for the clock, hostname and kernel logs.

The score in systemd-analyze security drops from 5.5 MEDIUM to 1.7 OK. Systems with mutable users are unchanged.

  • nixos/tests/accountsservice: test immutable users

Add a node with users.mutableUsers = false. Check that users can still set their icon, email and language, that every method that changes users is rejected, that /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group do not change, and that the daemon cannot write to /etc or home folders. Check that users can still be created, renamed and deleted on the node with mutable users.

items.content_html:
This is now a transitive dependency of flatpak, which was previously buildable for musl.

Things done

  • Built on platform(s)
    • x86_64-linux
    • aarch64-linux
    • x86_64-darwin
    • aarch64-darwin
  • For non-Linux: Is sandboxing enabled in nix.conf? (See Nix manual)
    • sandbox = relaxed
    • sandbox = true
  • Tested, as applicable:
    • NixOS test(s) (look inside nixos/tests)
    • and/or package tests
    • or, for functions and "core" functionality, tests in lib/tests or pkgs/test
    • made sure NixOS tests are linked to the relevant packages
  • Tested compilation of all packages that depend on this change using nix-shell -p nixpkgs-review --run "nixpkgs-review rev HEAD". Note: all changes have to be committed, also see nixpkgs-review usage
  • Tested basic functionality of all binary files (usually in ./result/bin/)
  • 25.05 Release Notes (or backporting 24.11 and 25.05 Release notes)
    • (Package updates) Added a release notes entry if the change is major or breaking
    • (Module updates) Added a release notes entry if the change is significant
    • (Module addition) Added a release notes entry if adding a new NixOS module
  • Fits CONTRIBUTING.md.

Add a 👍 reaction to pull requests you find important.
